cards.text: Some time later, war breaks out at a place called Gezer. No rest for the warriors, friend. They're like my oven timer: the second one goes off, another one starts.

cards.question: A new war breaks out at Gezer. Who is Israel fighting this time?

cards.text: At Gezer, Sibbecai the Hushathite, one of David's mighty men (1 Chronicles 11:29), faces Sippai, a descendant of the Rephaim. Sibbecai versus Sippai: say THAT five times fast while somebody's swinging at you.

cards.question: At Gezer, Sibbecai the Hushathite kills Sippai, a descendant of the Rephaim.
Sippai goes down at Gezer, and the Philistines are ___.

cards.text: Once again, there's a battle with the Philistines. This time, Elhanan son of Jair goes up against a man named Lahmi.

cards.question: Lahmi, the Philistine Elhanan faces, has a famous brother. Who is he?

cards.text: Yes, THAT Goliath, the Philistine David took down with a sling and a stone (1 Samuel 17:50).
The verse also mentions a spear with a shaft like a weaver's beam. Friend, that's not a spear, that's a fence post that got a job.
And there's ALSO a battle at Gath. There's a man there of great stature, and something about him is very unusual.

cards.question: What's unusual about the man of great stature at Gath?

answers.text: Six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot
A bronze coat of armor weighing five thousand shekels
An iron bed nine cubits long and four cubits wide

cards.question: The man at Gath has six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot. Add them all up and that's ___ in all.

cards.text: TWENTY-FOUR fingers and toes, and here I am packing cookie boxes with ONE mustache! He too was descended from Rapha, and he taunts Israel.

cards.question: The man of great stature taunts Israel at Gath. Who kills him?

cards.text: And Shimei is David's brother, so that's David's own nephew stepping up. Talk about keeping it in the family.

cards.question: So these descendants of Rapha in Gath fall at the hands of ___ and his ___.

findings.problem: The opening card gives no context. The passage starts mid-account with 'Some time later', but the card never says that this is Israel in David's day or what came before. It only names a place. The baker isn't told who is fighting or what is going on.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on. If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.

findings.problem: The timer joke says the moment one war ends another starts, with 'No rest for the warriors.' The verse says 'Some time later', so the joke works against the time the text gives. The joke also leans on an earlier war the baker hasn't been told about in this lesson, so the comparison doesn't land.

rule.text: A callback only works if its setup came earlier in this lesson or conversation.

findings.problem: No card ever says that Elhanan kills Lahmi (1 Chronicles 20:5). Card 6 says Elhanan 'goes up against' Lahmi, and cards 7 to 9 move on to Goliath and the spear. The outcome of the second battle, a key event in the passage, is never told or asked.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: Half the choice cards are pure discovery questions with no context to reason from: card 2 (the Philistines), card 7 (Goliath), card 11 (six fingers and toes) and card 14 (Jonathan son of Shimei). That is 4 of 8 choice cards, so informed guesses are not the majority. At least card 2 could become an informed guess with more setup on the opening card.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.
